description: Our team consists of a programmer, an engineer, and a graphic designer. We are a close-knit and highly motivated team, and we are only at the beginning of our journey. Together, we are developing an educational game focused on creating and completing missions inspired by NASA, combining technology, engineering, and creativity.
summary:
APOLLO turns Apollo-era engineering into a crew-first interactive experience. Players configure propulsion, life support, payload, and guidance systems, then see how their choices affect mission resources such as mass, power, oxygen, CO₂ scrubbing, and communications. After launch, they enter a 3D Command Module Columbia, respond to a cabin emergency, and decide how to handle the Apollo Guidance Computer’s 1202 alarm.

The experience connects spacecraft design with human consequences: every trade-off affects the crew’s safety, scientific goals, or chance of returning home. A mission report explains the outcome with telemetry, causal details, and comparisons to Apollo 11. An interactive field guide adds source-linked historical context.

Built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Three.js, APOLLO is designed as an educational prototype and a NASA Space Apps-style challenge project. Its systems and outcomes are simplified for play; it is not a certified flight model.
details:
Apollo 11 Mission Game
Challenge: Space Mission Design Game

Apollo 11 Mission Game is a browser-based, first-person 3D game that puts players inside the spacecraft. Players manage oxygen and other resources, repair instruments and make decisions that affect the crew’s survival and mission outcome.

Space missions balance objectives, spacecraft, instruments, power, mass, communications and budget. Students rarely experience these trade-offs through a complete mission. Our game makes them tangible through Apollo 11, a familiar mission with a fragile journey.

Players explore a low-poly retro spacecraft through short interactive scenes. They can inspect and repair instruments, track draining resources, and enlarge and rotate objects such as an oxygen cylinder. When oxygen runs low, the visor fogs. Players’ choices determine whether the mission succeeds or fails.

The objective is to reach the Moon and return safely. Resources are limited, and repair priorities and timing shape the result. This is an interactive mission simulation, not a story or quiz.

References: Apollo 11 Flight Journal · NASA Image and Video Library · Challenge · NASA Space Apps 2026

Technology: TypeScript and Next.js; runs in a browser without installation.
